chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Mufaddal, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A single man may perform Hajj on behalf of a single man, but a single woman may not perform Hajj on behalf of a single man.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: A person who has already performed their obligatory Hajj and is free from the obligation; literally 'single' or 'free'.

ai.seo_question: Can a single woman perform Hajj on behalf of a single man according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar highlights a nuanced asymmetry in Shia jurisprudence regarding Hajj on behalf of others, distinguishing between gender and marital status. While a free man may perform Hajj for another free man, a free woman is restricted from performing Hajj for a free man, reflecting scholarly discussions on the independence of female religious obligations versus their capacity to act as proxies for males in this specific ritual context.
